The Jug of Punch

A banjo-fiddle-piano version of this tune is included on the wonderful LIVE AT MONA‘S CD. A group of lower-eastside, NYC musicians in late-night session. Eamon O’Leary (banjo) and Patrick Ourceau (fiddle) lead the procedings on this one…

↳ Posted by oshea57 on October 31st, 2006.

Paddy Carty’s version

He plays one or two F#s I think. He also changes the rolls on c to cAc and cdc (or plays a roll on c instead of cdc) and plays d (breath) usually instead of the ~d3:

Re: The Jug Of Punch

X:5 is a transcription from Ddor to Edor of Tuttle’s Reel from Bobby Casey:
https://thesession.org/tunes/528
Comments at 528 confirm that there has been confusion between these two tunes.

Re: The Jug Of Punch

This should probably be a setting under https://thesession.org/tunes/594, not a new tune, shouldn’t it?

To elaborate on fiddlinggrapefruit’s suggestion, if the Ds and As are left major there’s a significant clash on F and C naturals that fall on the downbeat. If they’re just played “thirdless” (often noted as a chord like “D5”) the chords would be fine, but not major. Here’s a chordal arrangement that works, though there are a lot of other options:

X: 1
T: The Jug Of Punch
R: reel
M: 4/4
L: 1/8
K: Ddor
|:“Dm”A,DDC DEFG|AG G/G/G AcGF|“Am”EA,A,B, CDEF|“C”G2 AG FDEC|
“Dm”A,DDE FDDE|FDED CDEG|“C”cded cAGE|“Dm”FDEC D4:|
|:“Dm”Adde ~f3d|“Am”efed cAAG|“F”AGAB “C/G”cBcd|“Am”eaag “Dm”ed d2|
“Dm”Adde ~f3d|“Am”efed cAAB|“F”c3A “G”B2AG|“Dm”FDEC D4:|

↳ Posted by benhockenberry on April 18th, 2023.

The Jug Of Punch, X:11

Setting in G Dorian with change of octave avoiding the high notes using the low D as the lowest note.

I have had lots of fun today playing this with the Englitina, a mobile app created by Michael Eskin that simulates an English system concertina.

↳ Posted by Fernando Durbán Galnares on April 18th, 2023.

The Jug Of Punch, X:12

D dorian transposition from an E dorian setting in Darsie, Richard, 1996, Traditional Tune Sourcebook, vol. 1, Silver Sound Publications. Where I learned it. Distinctions are the high a in bar B4 and the (self-remonishing, guilt-tinged) B-flat in B7 (slide into it).

↳ Posted by Steve Moore on June 17th, 2023.
